title: Tom Preston-Werner and the Semantic Versioning Spec (c. 2009-2011)
explainer: Before Semantic Versioning existed, a version number like 2.5.1 meant whatever each project's maintainer felt like that week, which made 'install the right toolchain version' a genuine guessing game. GitHub cofounder Tom Preston-Werner wrote and published the SemVer specification - major.minor.patch, with explicit rules for what each number promises about compatibility - as an open, collaborative document around 2010, and ecosystems like npm and Rust's Cargo built it into their tooling from day one. That's why the version numbers you'll pin and compare in this lesson actually carry meaning instead of being arbitrary labels.
